Complementary Harness Rescue Training invokes this pool only when all initial attempts under the base harness fail. The same policy generates fresh rollouts under selected auxiliary harnesses, and these trajectories replace the failed group for reinforcement learning. An Adaptive Harness Router selects the Top-k variants using Harness Behavior Profiles and voting across multiple LLMs. Policy-aware profile re-anchoring refreshes this evidence as the policy learns. Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness. Behavioral analyses and held-out cases support the transfer of harness-elicited behaviors into the policy itself. Reusing the router for Rank-1 inference provides additional gains at the same executor rollout count.
title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training

enrich.summary_1line: VisSearch-Bench is a 204-task benchmark for long-horizon visual search by multimodal agents; the best system fully solves 26.47% of tasks.

text: Multimodal agents use web and image tools to answer questions beyond their internal knowledge. Some search tasks use images mainly to identify an initial entity, then rely on text retrieval. These tasks offer limited insight into how agents connect information across images, objects, and search steps. We therefore focus on visual context management. This involves organizing and using visual information and linking it to other findings during search. Visually intensive tasks require agents to combine object appearance, local details, or spatial relations with external information. We introduce VisSearch-Bench, with 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains. It covers Set-wise Visual Search, Sequential Visual Search, Hybrid Wide-Deep Search, Competitive Visual Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search. Each task provides a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules. Accuracy measures complete task success, while Process Score measures the correctness and completeness of individual results and subquestion answers. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solves only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools. These results highlight the challenge of linking visual evidence with search results to produce complete answers.
title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents

enrich.summary_1line: WeLM-Image is a unified text-to-image, editing, and multi-reference model designed for single-GPU deployment, per its authors.

text: We present WeLM-Image, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a 1024times1024 image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.
title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence

text: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanScale, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanScale-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models

text: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient and photorealistic head avatar reconstruction, yet monocular video-based or image-based methods still suffer from under-constrained geometry and texture, leading to artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability. We present EDGAR (Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement), a conditional diffusion framework designed to enhance the quality of Gaussian avatars by correcting artifacts while preserving identity fidelity. To train EDGAR, we construct EDGAR-SET, a hybrid triplet dataset composed of real-captured and synthetic-rendered samples, which simulates realistic Gaussian avatar failure cases by pairing degraded renderings with ground-truth and reference images. EDGAR refines degraded frames through a fusion block that injects identity features extracted by the self-supervised Sapiens model into a one-step diffusion backbone, enabling effective artifact removal without sacrificing efficiency. Our EDGAR model incorporates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture to address diverse degradation types and severity levels. The refined multi-view renderings are subsequently used as pseudo-targets to optimize a single underlying Gaussian avatar, so that the final avatar can be rendered without applying EDGAR to every output frame. Experiments on three different Gaussian avatar reconstruction methods, each evaluated under three different settings, show improvements in both perceptual and reconstruction measures over the raw outputs and an SDEdit-style refinement baseline. In addition, cross-view evaluation demonstrates improved calibrated consistency, while tests under large yaw and open-mouth expressions verify robustness under extreme settings. These results collectively indicate a useful operating regime for recoverable appearance artifacts. The code is available at https://kwanyun.github.io/edgar/
title: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure

enrich.summary_1line: BestRand is a benchmark-compression method that subsamples evaluation sets to reduce high-error tail risk, with self-reported gains over competitors.

label.reason: Cheap, stable benchmark compression for model evaluation; practical for eval cost.

text: Benchmark compression reduces the often prohibitive time and cost of model evaluation by evaluating models on a small benchmark subset that closely matches full-benchmark results. To quantify estimation error, we derive an accurate analytical approximation to the error distribution when estimating full-benchmark scores from a subset, showing that most subsets yield small errors, while a few produce much larger errors, resulting in a long-tailed distribution. This means random sampling alone can achieve surprisingly strong performance with high probability, but remains unstable due to rare large errors. We further show that this instability is inherent to modern foundation models and persists even as more models are evaluated. Based on these findings, we introduce BestRand, a stable and low-cost benchmark compression method that preserves the efficiency of random sampling while substantially reducing its high-error tail. We validate BestRand on 70+ text, multimodal, and agent benchmarks, and further extend it to VLA evaluation. Compared with competitive methods, BestRand reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and estimation error by 16.4% on average, while requiring only 51.3% of the construction cost. It further reduces OOD estimation error by 21.8% on average across score-range, model-family, and temporal shifts. Together, our theory provides practical guidance for understanding and predicting the accuracy and reliability of benchmark compression, while BestRand enables stable and accurate compression at low cost. The code and data are publicly available onhttps://github.com/George-Ling3/BestRand.
title: Random Is Almost Enough? Stable and Low-Cost Benchmark Compression via BestRand

enrich.summary_1line: D3D is a standalone diffusion drafter for asynchronous speculative decoding, reporting 5.00x and 5.71x speedups on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B.

text: Target-conditioned diffusion drafters predict candidate tokens in parallel, yet each new block must wait for updated target-model hidden states. This forces drafting and verification to run sequentially, limiting speedup even though each block is generated in one pass. We introduce D3D, a standalone diffusion drafter that removes this inter-round dependency. D3D combines blockwise denoising with auxiliary autoregressive supervision to achieve long accepted prefixes without target hidden states. This independence lets D3D draft successor blocks during verification in one packed pass, enabling asynchronous speculative decoding. We progressively prune layers according to their effect on acceptance length to reduce the cost of packed drafting. Removing five of 36 layers retains over 99\% of mean acceptance length across three benchmarks with Qwen3-8B as the target. Across seven benchmarks, D3D averages 5.00times and 5.71times decoding speedup with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B targets, compared with 4.03times and 3.67times for DFlash. On GSM8K with Qwen3-32B, speedup reaches 7.48times. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/fudan-generative-vision/D3D.
title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding

enrich.summary_1line: Halley is a predictive control plane framework for optical AI data center networks, reporting goodput gains in simulation.

text: A frontier AI model is trained in an AI data center, on tens of thousands of accelerators joined by a dedicated network, and every training step ends with all of them exchanging data at once. Between racks, that network is optical, and each of its four layers, from lasers to switches, runs a fixed or after-the-fact policy. Lasers sharing an enclosure, cooling, and power can fail together. At a fixed spare ratio, correlated failure provably caps a pool's availability however large it grows. In this paper, we present a comprehensive predictive control plane framework, called Halley, that reads each resource's next state and acts before the failure occurs. It has four components, each carrying a formal guarantee: LightReserve that sizes the laser pool to provide a coverage bound, FoldFit that schedules the switch within 11/9 of the optimal, ThermaLead that holds a microring with one-step-ahead control, and TriageGuard that protects the highest-risk modules first. Halley gives each layer a predictive controller that defers to the deployed policy when unsure. Composed from simulations at that point, effective goodput, the share of ideal throughput kept, rises from 65.2\% to 76.5\% if a window that exhausts its spares is lost. If only the dark channels' bandwidth is lost, it reaches 67.4\%. Per megawatt, that is up to 1.03--1.17 times the training; for the same training, up to 3.3--14.7\% less data center capacity. Halley's fallback circuits are formally verified and are shown to achieve close timing on a commercial FPGA, and pass a 130~nm signoff.
title: Halley: A Predictive Control Plane for Optical AI Data Center Networks

text: Streaming digital humans produce detailed video while continuing speech as new text arrives. High-resolution denoising is costly, and text updates can cause repeated or interrupted speech. We present TaoMate-HD, an autoregressive model for high-resolution audio-video streaming. For each short segment, or chunk, two denoising steps establish coarse video structure at low resolution. A final step refines the video to high resolution, with audio generated throughout the same trajectory. Each stage passes its audiovisual predictions to the same stage of the next chunk as history. Across text updates, the model retains this history to infer what has already been spoken. Continuation training utilizes asymmetric text conditioning, with separate text windows for generation and distillation. Experiments show a 1.6x speedup over direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Optimized stage-parallel deployment provides a further 1.9x overall speedup over serial progressive generation. Our continuation training reduces character error rate by 11.18 percentage points relative to the baseline. The model also supports hour-long audiovisual generation. Our project page is https://taoliveaigc.github.io/TaoMate-HD.
title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation

enrich.summary_1line: The SIMPLE paper proposes a four-parameter law predicting LLM inference energy, fit on 13 dense LLMs on NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

label.reason: Analytical model of LLM inference energy and cost driven by KV-cache; useful serving insight.

text: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.
title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference

enrich.summary_1line: The paper studies rewriting open-weight models' earlier reasoning into compact records, finding shorter future reasoning and, in some deployments, lower agent spending.

text: Reasoning substantially improves language models' ability to solve difficult problems, but long reasoning traces make these gains expensive. Efficient reasoning should express useful analysis in fewer tokens by reducing repetition and text that adds little value to solving the problem. Progress in proprietary models motivates this goal, yet their hidden scratchpads limit direct study of how it is achieved. We investigate whether open-weight models can generate less verbose reasoning by changing the form of their own earlier thoughts, without retraining. Our intervention rewrites prior reasoning into compact state records before pending tool results are revealed, then compares continuations from original and compact histories. Across the tested models, accepted compact histories usually shorten future reasoning; a coding case study also shows less repeated verification after a shared candidate solution. In software-agent deployments, compaction can reduce total spending, although task quality and rewrite-inclusive time depend on the target and compressor. These findings identify reasoning history as one way to reduce future reasoning-token use and motivate model-specific compaction policies evaluated for both efficiency and retained capability.
title: Why Pay for Long Reasoning When Rewrite Do Trick? Causal Effects of Reasoning History Compaction on Future Generation and Agent Cost

enrich.summary_1line: UniRestorer++ is an expert-routing image restoration framework with multi-granularity degradation modeling, plus a 50-category benchmark named CDD-50.

text: Universal image restoration aims to handle diverse degradations within a single model, but a reliable scaling strategy remains underexplored. Increasing backbone depth and width can lead to performance saturation, while degradation-aware specialization depends on accurate degradation estimation and is vulnerable to errors on out-of-distribution and real-world inputs. We propose UniRestorer++, a scalable framework based on multi-granularity degradation modeling. It progressively refines degradation groups and introduces group-specific experts, coupling capacity growth with specialization. Degradation-estimation-based routing selects a root-to-leaf path, while granularity-estimation-based routing chooses a level along that path to balance specialization and robustness. Spatially dense degradation representation maps further enable region-aware routing for spatially non-uniform corruptions. We develop CDD-50, a benchmark covering 50 degradation categories from single to penta-degradation. Experiments show approximately log-linear PSNR trends over the evaluated model-size range and stronger scaling gains on out-of-distribution and real-world data than vanilla MoE scaling. UniRestorer++ achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks and demonstrates zero-shot generalization and few-shot transfer on real-world images. Code: https://github.com/mrluin/UniRestorer_plusplus
title: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration with Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling

enrich.summary_1line: TAC-CoT interleaves latent reasoning segments with textual tool calls and answers, reporting up to 8.8-point accuracy gain and 6.8x fewer forward passes.

text: LLM-based agentic systems are increasingly combined with CoT reasoning to solve tasks that require accurate reasoning, external knowledge, and multi-step deliberation. Yet, explicit CoT incurs substantial generation overhead, while implicit CoT, which replaces textual rationales with compact continuous tokens, does not naturally support the explicit communication interface required for agentic tool-use. We propose TAC-CoT, a tool-empowered adaptive implicit CoT framework that replaces explicit reasoning traces with compact latent reasoning segments while retaining textual tokens only for tool calls, observations, and final answers. This interleaved design enables agentic tool-use without verbalizing every intermediate reasoning step. Experiments on agentic math and QA benchmarks show that TAC-CoT improves accuracy by up to 8.8 points while reducing model forward passes by up to 6.8x. Furthermore, analyses show that TAC-CoT improves tool-use quality in both single- and multi-tool settings.
title: TAC-CoT: Tool-Empowered Implicit Chain-of-Thought via Interleaving Explicit Tokens

enrich.summary_1line: NitroFusion2 is a diffusion distillation method that adds text-stream adversarial loss, targeting 1-2 step image generation.

text: Adversarial diffusion distillation has conventionally relied on image features for discrimination. We revisit this choice for multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs), whose text stream becomes image-dependent through joint attention. We introduce Text-Stream Adversarial Distillation (TSAD), which exploits intermediate text-token states as a new adversarial representation. Because the text stream has already read the image while remaining tied to the text condition, changing that condition changes what information it extracts from the image. Building on this property, we introduce Aspect-Cued Discrimination (ACD), which conditions the discriminator on different aspects of the sample, such as typography, objects, or style, to steer which properties are emphasized during adversarial training. Building on the expert-discriminator design of NitroFusion, we integrate TSAD and ACD in NitroFusion2. NitroFusion2 brings few-step distillation from the conventional 4-8-step regime down to just 1-2 steps at comparable quality. At one step, it produces sharp rendered text and rich fine-grained details, making one-step generation practical rather than merely a stress test for distillation. At two steps, it remains competitive across the evaluated benchmarks. These results establish the MMDiT text stream as a powerful and steerable representation for adversarial diffusion distillation.
title: NitroFusion2: Bringing Adversarial Loss to the Text Stream of Multimodal Diffusion Transformers

enrich.summary_1line: PyRUA-REAL is a framework where coding agents refine robot code from real-world exploration, reporting 91.1% success on eight real tasks.

label.reason: Coding agents with persistent memory and skills for robots; niche robotics application.

text: Coding agents powered by models such as GPT-6-Astra connect spatial reasoning with executable robot behavior, raising the question of how such agents can produce lasting improvements in robot capabilities from physical interaction. In this work, we study embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) through real-world exploration, code refinement, and deployment using PyRUA-REAL, a framework in which coding agents retain interaction experience as persistent memory and reusable executable skills that inform subsequent exploration and improvement. Our empirical study places physical manipulation at the center of the improvement process, examining how agents collaborate, what kinds of execution feedback support effective code refinement, and how task specifications and previously acquired skills influence robustness and task transfer. We further investigate the efficiency and capability of the resulting programs when deployed without involving an online agent for decision-making. Across eight real-world tasks, PyRUA-REAL achieves an average success rate of 91.1%. In complementary evaluation on 42 tasks from the RoboDojo benchmark, it achieves an average success rate of 84.4%. This study provides empirical guidance for turning physical exploration into reusable robot skills that support continued improvement and robust, efficient deployment.
title: PyRUA-REAL: Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning through RSI in the Real World

text: Probabilistic time-series forecasting requires models that simultaneously capture structured temporal dynamics, expressive uncertainty, and efficient inference, yet existing approaches fall short of this goal: latent dynamical models impose structure but rely on restrictive generation mechanisms, while modern generative methods such as diffusion and flow matching achieve flexibility at the cost of iterative and computationally expensive sampling. We introduce the Koopman Generative Operator (KGO), a probabilistic forecasting method that conceptualizes prediction as the evolution of structured uncertainty. KGO integrates three core components: (1) Koopman Patch Embedding (KoPE) for temporally consistent latent trajectory extrapolation; (2) Koopman Flow Matching (KoFM), which enables fast, single-step generation through a closed-form matrix exponential in a Koopman latent space, bypassing iterative sampling; and (3) an Adaptive Uncertainty Gate (AUG), which provides probabilistic forecasts by adapting uncertainty per-variable and per-horizon, corresponding to a learned decomposition of aleatoric uncertainty without manual tuning. By unifying these components, KGO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on 13/17 ProbTS benchmarks in CRPS and 16/17 in NMAE. Further, by eliminating iterative sampling, KGO delivers at least a 25times reduction in inference time compared to iterative generative models. These results position KGO as a practical and principled framework that advances the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in probabilistic time-series forecasting, combining leading accuracy on the evaluated benchmarks with fast, single-step generation.
title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

enrich.summary_1line: Paper finds multi-turn agentic RL gains depend on interaction budgets and introduces BudgetMix RL, a budget-varying training variant.

entities: paper:what does multi-turn reinforcement learning really improve in llm agents?
text: While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T via Pass@(K,T), we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten. Besides, agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience. To mitigate the deployment risks caused by this budget dependence, we provide a preliminary discussion on the benefits and limitations of process supervision signals and introduce BudgetMix RL as an alternative that varies interaction budgets during training. Experiments demonstrate that BudgetMix RL achieves robust performance across diverse execution settings. Project Page: https://rethinking-agentic-rl.github.io/
title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?

enrich.summary_1line: LoopVQ is a sub-1-bit KV cache quantization method for looped transformers, with an SGLang implementation reported by the authors.

label.reason: Sub-1-bit KV cache quantization for looped transformers; directly inference/quantization, though architecture-specific.

text: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. We observe that the KV cache of looped models is highly redundant along the loop axis and that the loop steps differ substantially in their sensitivity to quantization. Based on these observations, we propose LoopVQ, a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that codes channels of multiple loop steps jointly, and fine-tunes the codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model. At 0.5 bits per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods for standard LLMs on general, long chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval tasks with Ouro and Huginn models. Its design is orthogonal to these methods, and combined with TaSQ, it retains much of the BF16 accuracy even at 0.25 bits per element. We also implement LoopVQ in SGLang, where it nearly halves the decode latency at a 32K-token context and raises the peak serving throughput by up to 4.3times and 6.1times on the 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro models compared to the BF16 baseline.
title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers

text: Key Changes Version 0.22.0 is a minor release because it adds substantial runtime hardening and tightens an existing provider configuration contract. Applications that combine an explicit openai_client with organization or project must move those values to the AsyncOpenAI client. Highlights: Redacts terminal function-tool output rejected by agent output guardrails from replayable and persisted SDK state. Raises ModelBehaviorError for non-streaming Responses with terminal status failed or incomplete . Rejects conflicting provider options when OpenAIProvider receives an explicit client. Isolates usage accounting between independent RunState checkpoints while preserving nested-agent aggregation. Expands agents registered through handoff(agent) in generated graphs. Clarifies the existing shallow-copy behavior of Agent.clone() and RealtimeAgent.clone() . text: What's Changed 🛡️ Security GHSA-m5vj-8mcw-82qx (high): web_fetch_tool and the WebFetch capability's local fallback re-indented a JSON response on the event loop before applying the returned-content limit, so a deeply nested document within the download size limit could expand to hundreds of times its size, using large amounts of memory and delaying other work in the same process. You are affected if an attacker can choose or influence the URLs the tool fetches. Provider-native web fetching is not affected. Fixed in v2.66.0 and v1.107.10 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). GHSA-mfx5-pc32-32m8 (high): The private_key pattern in Pydantic AI Harness's secret redaction backtracked exponentially on crafted text, so a few hundred characters that begin like a private key could occupy the event loop for minutes or longer. You are affected if you use redact_secrets or secret_data() with the private_key pattern, which is included by default, on text an attacker can influence. Fixed in pydantic-ai-harness 0.66.0. GHSA-5fj9-5pjw-vpwc (medium): The cloud-metadata blocklist that URL downloads check did not include Tencent Cloud's instance metadata address 169.254.0.23 , so someone who can supply a URL the application downloads could have it fetch the instance's temporary role credentials. You are affected if you run on Tencent Cloud and allow local URLs, through force_download='allow-local' on a FileUrl or web_fetch_tool(allow_local_urls=True) . Fixed in v2.66.0 and v1.107.10 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). GHSA-jp94-mmr3-2pvv (medium): With OpenTelemetry instrumentation enabled for embedding models, embedding spans recorded the extra_headers and extra_body embedding settings, so credentials passed through them could be read by anyone with access to the exported traces. You are affected if you instrument embedding models and pass secrets through those settings. Fixed in v2.66.0 and v1.107.10 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). Restrict access to historical traces and rotate credentials they exposed. GHSA-7494-925c-rrxv (medium): For models whose profile requires tool schemas without $defs and $ref , a small tool schema whose definitions reference one another repeatedly expanded exponentially when inlined on the event loop, which can take minutes of CPU time and gigabytes of memory. You are affected if you serve such a model through the AG-UI adapter, where clients submit their own frontend tool schemas. Fixed in v2.66.0 and v1.107.10 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). GHSA-484x-x9m4-62cj (medium): Decision models ( DecisionModel subclasses such as OpenAIDecisionsModel , and TypeSafeModel ) resolved every $ref in a tool's argument schema again at each place it appears, so a small crafted schema could take exponential time and memory on the event loop. You are affected if you use a decision model from v2.46.0 onward with tools whose schemas an attacker can supply, most directly through an AG-UI endpoint. Fixed in v2.66.0 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). GHSA-r879-rxgj-3g75 (medium): The Vercel AI and AG-UI adapters took time that grows with the square of the number of parts to load a submitted message, on the event loop, so a single request could delay other work in the same process. You are affected if you pass client-submitted conversations to VercelAIAdapter or AGUIAdapter . Fixed in v2.66.0 and v1.107.10 ( pydantic-ai , pydantic-ai-slim ). GHSA-4cj4-hgwf-4hc4 (medium): When message history was serialized and loaded again, a tool result containing a JSON object in the serialized shape of one of Pydantic AI's file types was rebuilt as that file. A third party who controls data a tool returns could use this to make the application download a URL on its local network, or make the model provider read an s3:// object or uploaded file with the application's credentials. You are affected if tool results can contain data third parties control, that history is stored and reloaded, held on the server by a UI adapter, or carried by Temporal, D

enrich.summary_1line: Hugging Face Transformers v5.22.0 adds Mistral Large 4, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters per token, plus FP8 adapter training support.

label.reason: Mistral Large 4: 1T-parameter MoE multimodal model with 49B active, supported in transformers; major LLM release.

text: New Models Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe. Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union. Key Features Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices: ~1T total / ~52B active parameters : granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert. 1M context length , for long-context workloads. Multimodal input : accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. Instruct and Reasoning functionalities with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request. Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities: Reasoning Mode : three reasoning efforts — low , medium , high (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run. Vision : analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights. Multilingual : natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union. System Prompt : strong adherence and support for system prompts. Agentic : native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement. Cybersecurity : state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests. Large Context Window : supports a 1M context window. The model is released under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License : a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. Recommended Settings Reasoning Effort : 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' — default is 'high' . Use reasoning_effort="high" for complex prompts and agentic usage, 'low' for fast chat replies and 'medium' for day to day usage. Sampling : for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: temperature=1.0 top_p=0.95 System Prompt : define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. Tools : keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. Context : the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. Breaking changes 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file ( #49679 ) by @3outeille Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and is_trainable is now True . Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. Separately, the AMD CI image now install FP8 backward: chunked expert dequant, skip autograd.Function at inference ( #50117 ) by @ArthurZucker in [ #50117 ] Train adapters on top of FP8 weights ( #50031 ) by @qgallouedec in [ #50031 ] [AMD CI] Install onnxscript, bitsandbytes and peft in the AMD image ( #50046 ) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [ #50046 ] Bugfixes and improvements Processor unnecessary warnings ( #49812 ) by @zucchini-nlp in [ #49812 ] Fix boolean padding in ClapFeatureExtractor ( #23648 ) ( #49960 ) by @rudy-07 in [ #49960 ] [Fix] Count cropping of an uninitialized layer as a no-op ( #50104 ) by @remi-or in [ #50104 ] [loading]

enrich.summary_1line: Transformers v5.20.0 adds Muse Spark Open, Ling 3.0 Flash, Kolibri 1, MiniCPM-V 4.7, UnlimitedOcr, UltraBERT and MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize, and lists breaking changes.

text: Release v5.20.0 New Model additions Muse Spark Open Muse Spark Open is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta that takes text, images, audio, and video as input and generates text. It has 816B total parameters (42B active per token) and a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens shared across modalities. It is trained for agentic coding tasks such as multi-file editing, debugging, and tool use. Checkpoints are available in BF16 and NVFP4 formats. Links: Documentation | Blog Post Add Muse Spark Open ( #49644 ) by @guarin in #49644 Ling 3.0 Ling 3.0 Flash is a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts language model from InclusionAI. Its decoder groups five Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers with one Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) layer. The MLA blocks use interleaved rotary embeddings and a head-wise output gate, and the feed-forward blocks combine routed and shared experts. It is natively supported in Transformers as BailingHybridForCausalLM , so it loads without trust_remote_code=True . Links: Documentation [Model] Add native Ling 3.0 Flash support ( #49446 ) by @icavan in #49446 Kolibri1 Kolibri 1 is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts reasoning model, focused on German and English. Each of its 50 layers routes every token to 6 of 384 experts using sigmoid routing, and adds one shared expert. Four sliding-window attention layers alternate with one full-attention layer, and RoPE is applied only in the sliding-window layers. Links: Documentation Add Kolibri 1 ( #49463 ) by @lucamotz in #49463 MiniCPM-V 4.7 MiniCPM-V is a series of efficient multimodal large language models developed by OpenBMB . Like MiniCPM-V 4.6, the MiniCPM-V 4.7 architecture pairs a SigLIP vision encoder that has a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model backbone, and supports both 4x and 16x visual downsampling modes. The main addition over 4.6 is canvas M-RoPE : instead of numbering visual tokens along a single 1-D sequence, the model lays every image out on a 2-D canvas and assigns each visual token a (temporal, height, width) position, so slices of the same image keep their spatial relationship and video frames keep their temporal order. Fix more stuff ( #48979 ) by @zucchini-nlp in #48979 UnlimitedOcr UnlimitedOcr is a single 3B-parameter OCR model from Baidu with a standard 32,768-token context length. It builds on DeepSeek OCR and replaces all decoder attention layers with Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA). This keeps the KV cache constant during decoding, so the model can transcribe dozens of pages in a single forward pass. It supports "gundam" mode (640x640 tiles with dynamic cropping) and "base" mode (a single 1024x1024 view), and it can output region detections with bounding boxes. Links: Documentation | Paper Add Unlimited OCR ( #46836 ) by @guarin in #46836 UltraBERT UltraBERT is a family of bidirectional text encoders trained with a combination of masking ratios, pruning, and distillation for classification and retrieval tasks. The released encoders support sequences of up to 32,768 tokens. They use rotary position embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, and alternating local and global attention (every third layer is global). Checkpoints include UltraBERT-150M and UltraBERT-380M for masked language modeling and fine-tuning, and UltraBERT-Embed-150M for text embeddings. Links: Documentation | Paper Integrate the UltraBERT architecture ( #49596 ) by @tomaarsen in #49596 MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B is an end-to-end audio understanding model for long-form multi-speaker transcription, speaker diarization, and timestamps. It combines a Whisper-style encoder, a 4× frame merge step, a multi-modal projector, and a Qwen3 language model. It produces joint transcription and diarization in a single pass, with segments formatted as [start][S01]text[end] . It supports long-form audio through Whisper-window chunking in the processor, promptable transcription with hotword biasing, and 50+ languages. Links: Doc

text: Release v5.19.0 New Model additions EmbeddingGemma2 EmbeddingGemma 2 is a multimodal embedding model from Google built on the Gemma 4 architecture. It encodes text, images, audio, and video, individually or combined in one input, into a shared 768-dimensional vector space for cross-modal retrieval, semantic similarity, clustering, and classification. It uses Matryoshka Representation Learning, so embeddings can be truncated to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions. It also offers configurable visual and video token budgets, and unused vision or audio towers can be disabled at load time to save memory. enrich.summary_1line: Transformers 5.18.0 adds Nemotron 3 Diarization, NemotronH Omni, HyperCLOVAX Vision V2 and GTE models, plus breaking changes and bug fixes.

label.reason: Open-weight speaker diarization model added to transformers; audio niche, outside his focus.

text: New Model additions Nemotron 3 Diarization Nemotron 3 Diarization is an open-weight streaming speaker diarization model designed to determine "who spoke when" in real-world audio. It supports both streaming and offline inference, handles up to eight speakers, and orders speaker outputs by each speaker's first arrival in the input audio. The model uses the Arrival-Order Speaker Cache (AOSC) 1 and FIFO queue introduced for Streaming Sortformer 1 , 2 . A single checkpoint supports configurable latency profiles, from an 80 ms input buffer to a 30.4 s offline-style buffer, and configurable output frame resolution in multiples of 10 ms. With chunked inference, the maximum audio duration is not limited. Links: Documentation Add Nemotron3Diarization ( #49056 ) by @eustlb in #49056 NemotronH Omni NemotronH Omni is a multimodal reasoning model from NVIDIA that pairs the NemotronH hybrid Mamba-Transformer language model with a RADIO vision encoder and an optional Parakeet-based sound encoder. Image (and video) patches are projected through a RADIO tower and a pixel-shuffle MLP into the language model's embedding space at the <image> / <video> context-token positions; audio clips are projected in the same way at <audio> positions. The result is a single autoregressive model that reasons jointly over text, images, video and sound. Links: Documentation Add support for Nemotron Omni ( #46509 ) by @meatybobby in #46509 HyperCLOVAX Vision V2 HyperCLOVAX Vision V2 is a multimodal vision-language model developed by NAVER. It combines the HyperClovaX language model backbone with a Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder. The model supports text, image, and video inputs and is capable of chain-of-thought reasoning via built-in thinking tokens ( <think>...</think> ). Links: Documentation add HyperClovaX Vision ( #44314 ) by @jp1924 in #44314 GTE GTE was proposed in mGTE: Generalized Long-Context Text Representation and Reranking Models for Multilingual Text Retrieval by Xin Zhang, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Wen Xie, Ziqi Dai, Jialong Tang, Huan Lin, Baosong Yang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Meishan Zhang, Wenjie Li and Min Zhang. GTE is a BERT-style bidirectional encoder that replaces absolute position embeddings with RoPE, uses a gated MLP, and applies layer normalization after each residual connection. The same architecture backs Alibaba's gte-*-v1.5 , gte-multilingual-* and gte-en-mlm-* checkpoints as well as Snowflake's snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0 .
